title: Refactor scheduler: make workload signals explicit (prompt length buckets, concurrency) for tier mapping
author: Lena Fischer
description:
Context: Tiered batching defaults (fast/standard/cost_efficient) need a stable set of workload signals so the tier mapping is explainable, testable, and consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Prior to this PR, the scheduler inferred “shape” of a request from scattered fields (raw prompt token count, route hints, a few ad-hoc moving averages) and the tier mapping logic reached into scheduler internals to fetch them. That made it hard to reason about regressions (e.g., streaming cadence issues) and hard to add new signals safely.

This PR refactors the serving scheduler API to expose an explicit WorkloadSignals struct (prompt-length buckets, concurrency estimate, streaming/non-streaming, and basic context flags) computed at admission time and updated on a bounded cadence. Tier mapping now consumes WorkloadSignals rather than ad-hoc scheduler state, and we document the contract + add unit/integration tests to prevent silent behavior changes.

Key changes (high level):
- Introduce WorkloadSignals as a first-class input to tier mapping:
  - prompt_len_bucket: {0-256, 257-1k, 1k-4k, 4k+} (token-based, post-normalization)
  - concurrency_bucket: {1, 2-4, 5-8, 9-16, 17+} (derived from active decode slots per model replica, EWMA-smoothed)
  - streaming: boolean
  - long_context: boolean (based on model context window + request max_input_tokens)
  - route_class: {chat, completions, embeddings, rerank} (used only for guardrails; no bespoke scheduling)
- Move signal computation to admission + per-replica sampler:
  - Admission computes request-local fields (prompt_len_bucket, streaming, long_context)
  - Replica sampler computes concurrency_bucket from active work + queue depth, updated every 250ms (bounded overhead)
  - Tier mapping reads signals via SchedulerContext (no internal pointers to queues)
- Replace prior implicit thresholds with a documented contract:
  - Adds scheduler/docs/workload_signals.md describing buckets, update frequency, and what is/isn’t stable
  - Adds a “compatibility notes” section for mapping logic (so future changes require explicit review)
- Tests:
  - Unit tests for bucket boundary behavior (exactly-at-boundary cases)
  - Determinism tests: same input signals => same effective tier parameters
  - Integration tests validating signals show up in trace spans and in /config/explain payloads (paired with PR #18470)

Motivation / why now:
- Unblocks ongoing tier default tuning work by giving us a stable input surface for parameter mapping (see ENG-18421).
- Makes perf canary failures diagnosable by recording bucketed signals alongside queue delay/batch formation metrics (ENG-18422).
- Reduces coupling between tier mapping and scheduler internals, enabling safer future scheduler refactors.

Implementation notes:
- Buckets are intentionally coarse to avoid per-request jitter and minimize PII/trace concerns.
- Concurrency_bucket uses an EWMA over active decode slots; we avoid using instantaneous queue depth alone to prevent thrash under bursty traffic.
- For streaming requests, WorkloadSignals.streaming is set at admission and never changes; tier mapping can choose more conservative queue delay defaults.

Example (illustrative) snippet:
- Before: tier_mapper::select_params(model, req, scheduler_state*)
- After:  tier_mapper::select_params(model, req, const WorkloadSignals&)

Rollout / risk:
- This is intended to be behavior-preserving with respect to effective tier parameters for the existing supported workloads.
- Guarded by existing tier feature flag paths (no new flags introduced). The main risk is bucket boundary changes altering tier parameter selection in edge cases.
- Added trace annotations so we can compare “old vs new” behavior on staging by replaying identical traffic and diffing signals/params.

Follow-ups:
- Consider adding a separate bucket for ultra-long prompts (8k+) once long-context model rollout expands.
- Wire WorkloadSignals into perf canary reporting tables to correlate regressions with buckets (tracked in ENG-18423).

Release note: none (internal refactor; surfaced only via trace fields and docs for internal developers).

runtime/admission: compute request-local workload signals (prompt_len_bucket, streaming, long_context)
runtime/tier_mapper: refactor to consume WorkloadSignals; remove scheduler internals dependency
runtime/tracing: annotate spans with workload signal buckets
docs(runtime): add workload_signals contract doc + mapping notes
tests: bucket boundary unit tests + tier mapping determinism tests

conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): The concurrency signal definition needs to be explicit about update cadence and what happens when sampler stalls. Please document and add a test that sampler lag doesn’t cause unbounded staleness.

Lena Fischer (author): Added docs section “Update frequency + staleness bounds” (250ms tick, clamp at 2s; if sampler stalls we mark concurrency_bucket=unknown and tier mapper falls back to standard defaults). Added unit test for fallback path.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Bucket boundaries: why 256/1k/4k? We’ve seen 512-token prompts dominate some chat workloads. Can we avoid overfitting?

Lena Fischer (author): Boundaries chosen to align with prefill cost regimes we already use in benchmark sweeps; they’re coarse and stable. Added note that boundaries are contract-stable for v1; can revise only with explicit perf + SRE signoff. Also added a test to keep boundary constants in one place.
Julian Moore (review): Please ensure trace annotations are low-cardinality and do not include raw counts. Also add a regression test that we don’t accidentally log token counts.
Lena Fischer (author): Trace fields are enum buckets only (e.g., prompt_len_bucket=1k_4k). Added a unit test that serialization path rejects raw token_count labels in WorkloadSignals.
Noah Patel (review): This refactor touches scheduler interfaces—any downstream call sites in Private installer or older runtime branches?

Lena Fischer (author): All changes are within runtime; public config schema unchanged. Verified release/* branches unaffected; no external API. Added compile-time adapter for a deprecated internal call to keep older modules building until we land PR #18515 backports.
Ethan Park (review): /config/explain payload: make sure the new fields are behind the same capability gating as other debug metadata. Some customers can view explain in Console.
Lena Fischer (author): Gated workload_signals fields behind existing ‘config_explain_metadata’ capability and redacted route_class unless internal (hosted staff). Added tests.
Sofia Ivanova (final): Looks good. Please rerun perf sanity; last run showed a small p95 drift on streaming routes.
Lena Fischer (author): Reran staging replay + perf smoke. Drift was from a test harness mismatch; updated harness to pin bucket calculation to normalized tokenization. Latest perf smoke within noise.
